# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)

Diagnosed cand_0002's (champion) trials from `./trajectories/` (33 trials, 11 val tasks). **Exactly 1 imperfect trial exists**: case-030-real-operator-structured-logging t0 (task mean 0.92; t1/t2 score 5/5). All 32 other trials score full. No ENVIRONMENT faults. Max recoverable ≈ +0.008 val (0.992 → 1.0).

| rank | cluster | task (trial) | shared root cause | tag | change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Review-driven work-type split of a shared-surface enforcement deliverable → unmanaged size overage + unrecorded bundling (dq 4/5) | case-030 (t0) | The internal review docked Criterion 3 (E001 over the ~2-week guideline) and issued a split suggestion; the revise executed the old "Oversized epic: split by sub-deliverable" playbook entry by carving the CI lint rule into standalone E004 (title "CI lint rule enforcing structured reconciliation log fields", `implementation_type: null`, same component as E001/E002). E001 stayed over guideline; the grader docked exactly that ("the size remains above guideline, which the embedded adversarial review also docked") plus the HLR-7 P1-into-P0 bundling recorded only as scattered prose, not on the matrix row. Passing siblings t1/t2 keep 3 epics with the lint rule **divided per binary into the consuming epics** (t1's summary: "the DAG issue was resolved by making the lint coverage per-binary (each implementation epic authors and verifies the lint") and the bundling flagged in-row (`E001 (bundled)` + rationale) or as a self-contained Step-4 analysis — shapes the graders quote in their 5/5 rationales | BEHAVIORAL (churn instruction in the revise playbook) + KNOWLEDGE (recording contracts) | STRUCTURAL: new validator check 6 (work-type-extracted enforcement deliverable) + generation rule + review classification + revise playbook replacement |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)

All edits target cluster 1 (the only failing cluster). Structurally different from every rejected batch: cand_0003 (prose recording mandates), cand_0005/0006 (validator checks enforcing the *recording* of the 4-epic shape), cand_0007 (prose shape rules, no code enforcement). This batch combines the shape-level rules with **mechanical code enforcement of the epic SHAPE itself** — the lever no prior batch used.

| # | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | STRUCTURAL (bundled script) | `epic-decompose/scripts/validate_decomposition.py` — new check 6 | A general Implementation epic whose **title** names an enforcement tool (lint rule / CI check / static-analysis check / validation harness) that shares its `component` with ≥1 other non-docs Implementation epic is a work-type extraction → VIOLATION with paste-ready fold-back FIX (divide per surface into consuming epics' Scope/ACs, delete the epic, update the summary). Fires at decompose Step 8c, review Step 1.7, and revise Step 4 — so it catches the extraction at every phase, including when the REVISE creates it (which is when t0's E004 appeared) | Yes — corpus-verified: an Epic-List title scan over all 33 trials finds an enforcement-titled epic in EXACTLY case-030 t0; the negative fixture (enforcement tool as the component's only implementation work) is explicitly exempt |
| 2 | KNOWLEDGE + worked example (generation rule) | `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 5, Epic Boundary Rules, new sub-bullet | Shared-surface enforcement deliverables divide per surface into the consuming epics' Scope/ACs, never a standalone work-type epic; worked example (per-binary lint ownership + mirror AC); explicit exemption when the enforcement tool IS the component's only implementation work | Yes — fires only when a shared enforcement deliverable exists (only t0 in the corpus); t1/t2 already produce the mandated per-surface shape |
| 3 | CONTRACT (recording) | `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 6.5 | An epic kept above the ~2-week guideline as one logical change must record estimate + why-not-split rationale + **concrete conditional re-split trigger** in Health Warnings — the t1/t2 grader-quoted shape; a bare size note is named as the defect | Yes — fires only when an overage is kept (only t0 in the corpus); passing size-flagged trials already write trigger-style conditionals (case-019 t1, case-020 t1, case-030 t1/t2 — journal-verified in cand_0003's entry) |
| 4 | CONTRACT (recording) | `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 4 | A kept lower-priority-into-higher-priority bundling must be readable from the HLR Traceability Matrix row itself (`(bundled)` flag + inline rationale) or a self-contained note; bare-pointer rows named as the defect shape | Yes — fires only in the bundling branch; corpus check: passing bundling trials (case-016 ×3, 017-t1, 018-t2, 029 ×3, 030 t1/t2) record in-row flags or self-contained notes (grep-verified); t0's prose-only acknowledgment is the only bare shape |
| 5 | CONTRACT (sync) | `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 8c | Validator description now includes check 6 and its fix path | Yes — additive description |
| 6 | STRUCTURAL (review mapping) | `prompts/review-agent.md` Step 1.7 | Check-6 violation → **minor** Epic-Boundaries issue (the one validator violation that does NOT zero a criterion — directionally right, mechanical fold-back) with the named correction | Yes — issues added only on violations; minor severity cannot fail a passing review |
| 7 | KNOWLEDGE (review classification) | `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 3 | Size check CLASSIFIES before flagging: heterogeneous monolith → major split demand (preserved — case-029 t0's shape); one-logical-change overage with trigger → watch item, no dock; trigger absent → minor "record the trigger"; standalone enforcement epic → minor "divide per surface". Un-actionable "consider splitting" suggestions forbidden — the exact suggestion whose execution caused t0's churn chain | Yes — only case-030 t0's review ever docked for size (journal-verified in cand_0005's entry); heterogeneous-monolith split demand explicitly preserved |
| 8 | STRUCTURAL (revise playbook) | `prompts/revise-agent.md` | REPLACED "Oversized epic: Split by sub-deliverable" (the churn instruction) with a 3-shape classified fix (monolith split / keep+trigger / fold-back); NEW mechanical entry for check-6 violations (fold per surface, delete the epic, update summary); NEW minor-issue corrections "record the re-split trigger" and "record the bundling rationale in the matrix row" (both do-not-restructure) | Yes — revise only acts on review issues; the corrections are the grader-endorsed remedies; case-029 t0's monolith split path is preserved verbatim in branch (a) |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/new-rule now does on those exact inputs)

- **Validator check 6** — `--self-check` passes (fires on a standalone-enforcement-epic fixture with same-component siblings; clean when the enforcement tool is the component's only implementation epic). Simulated end-to-end on t0's reconstructed final shape (E001/E002 implementation + E004 "CI lint rule enforcing structured reconciliation log fields", all component "OpenShift AI Productization", frontmatter read from the t0 trace): exits 1 with "RHAISTRAT-8010-E004: standalone enforcement deliverable … divide the enforcement deliverable per surface into each consuming epic's Scope and Acceptance Criteria, delete this epic". Corpus: an Epic-List title scan over all 33 trials finds an enforcement-titled epic in EXACTLY case-030 t0 — no false positives possible on the other 32 trials regardless of component.
- **trace case-030 t0 (grader: "the size remains above guideline, which the embedded adversarial review also docked")** → with the edits the chain is broken at three points: (i) the review's Criterion 3 classification forbids the un-actionable split suggestion and instead demands the trigger/minor corrections; (ii) if a split is nevertheless attempted, revise Step 4's validator run exits 1 on the standalone lint epic and the new playbook entry folds it back per surface (the t1 5/5 shape, which t1's summary explicitly documents); (iii) the kept-overage path now records estimate + rationale + re-split trigger, the shape the t2 grader quoted at 5/5 ("records a concrete re-split trigger if the audit exceeds the 75% estimate. This is a defensible trade-off, not a monolith gap").
- **trace case-030 t0 (grader: HLR-7 bundling "not covered by a triage escape", recorded only in prose)** → Step 4's row-flag contract + review Criterion 3's bundling-recording check (minor) + the revise's "record in matrix row" correction land the `(bundled)` flag + inline rationale — exactly t1's matrix row ("E001 (bundled) | Bundled with P0 work: `resourceKind` is added to the same log ca…") that the t1 grader quoted at 5/5. Corpus check: t0 is the only trial whose bundling lives solely in scattered prose (t1 in-row, t2 self-contained note; 016/017/018/029 record flags/notes).
- **Blast radius (all edits, BOUNDED)**: every edit fires only under a discriminator — enforcement-titled epic with same-component siblings (only t0), kept overage (only t0), kept bundling (passing trials already produce the accepted shapes) — verified against the 33-trial corpus as above. Passing tasks named in the class: case-013/014/015/016/017/018/019/020/024/029 and case-030 t1/t2; none produces a shape any new rule flags or demands changed.

## Process & features used

- Serial (no subagents/worktrees): a single failing cluster with one coherent mechanism; the 9 edits span 5 files whose contents must stay mutually consistent (validator ↔ decompose Step 5/6.5/8c ↔ review 1.7/Criterion 3 ↔ revise playbook) — parallel edit-subagents would have conflicted.
- Corpus reconstruction: extracted all 33 trials' final artifacts (Write/Edit replay) + Read tool_results for Bash-created files (frontmatter is set via `scripts/frontmatter.py`, so epic frontmatter was read from late-trace Read results) into /tmp for scanning.
- Read: `guidance/skill-package/SKILL.md` (levers: skipped-step→bundled-script, output-contract, worked example), `guidance/diagnose/SKILL.md`, JOURNAL RESULT lines for all 7 prior iterations, rejected.jsonl.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)

- The validator's checks 1-5 (judge parity) and their decompose-8c / review-1.7 / revise-4 wiring — unchanged this iteration.
- Check 6's two-part discriminator (enforcement TITLE + same-component sibling). Broadening it to body-text matching or dropping the sibling condition would risk false positives on passing trials.
- The Criterion 3 heterogeneous-monolith split demand (case-029 t0 relies on it).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)

- Grader-side dq 4-vs-5 variance beyond the two named gaps — no prompt defect to fix; the recording/shape contracts are the strongest available lever against it (same conclusion as cand_0003/0005/0006/0007 handovers).
- Mandated-AC (Rules 24/25) validator prep — that judge is staged thresholdless; not REAL.
- Any change to SKILL.md dispatch/wave logic, fetch-agent.md — no failures in those phases.

## Environment faults

None. All 33 trials ran to completion; the single failure is a capability failure.
